subject: DPA redlines & audit evidence request — Aventis Health
messages:
From: Aventis Legal <contracts@aventis-health.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: DPA - initial redlines + audit scope question

Hi Neha,

Attached are our DPA redlines (see Aventis_DPA_redlines_v2.pdf). A few points we want to confirm before we move to signature:
- Audit rights: we expect standard annual SOC 2 review plus the option for an independent auditor with 30 days' notice for mission-critical data flows.
- Subprocessors: we'd like an explicit list of current subprocessors and a 30-day notice window for additions.
- Cross-border transfers: please confirm where data will be processed and whether you use any EU standard contractual clauses for transfers.

Can you confirm Redwood can provide SOC 2 Type II attestation and a high-level pen-test summary? If you accept the redlines we'd prefer DocuSign for execution.

Thanks,
Daniel Park
Senior Counsel, Aventis Health
[Attachment: Aventis_DPA_redlines_v2.pdf]
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Aventis Legal <contracts@aventis-health.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: DPA - initial redlines + audit scope question

Hi Daniel — thanks for sending this over and for the clear asks. Looping in Marissa (Legal) and Karthik (Privacy/Compliance) to review the redlines and confirm evidence.

High-level responses:
- SOC 2 Type II: we can provide our 2026 SOC 2 attestation (summary deliverable, full report under NDA).
- Pen test: we have a 2026 external penetration test summary we can share, redacted for sensitive details.
- Subprocessors: we maintain a live subprocessor inventory and can provide an export; notice window is typically 14 days but we can discuss 30 days for this engagement.
- Cross-border transfers: Redwood's hosted runtime has processing in us-west-2 and eu-west-1; for EU data we can add SCCs or use a private deployment option.

Marissa/Karthik — can you take point on the DPA redlines and confirm which items we can accept vs. ask to narrow? Goal is to get to DocuSign within two weeks.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Legal Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 10:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: DPA - initial redlines + audit scope question

Thanks Neha — quick read of their redlines attached. Key notes:
1) Audit rights: Aventis' proposed text is broader than our standard (they want independent auditor access). We can accept annual SOC 2 review plus a point-in-time independent audit right limited to 1x per 12 months, scoped to systems that process Aventis data, with mutual NDA and pre-approved audit firm.
2) Subprocessors: we will provide the live inventory export. For notice window we typically do 14 days; to meet them halfway, propose 21 days plus an emergency clause for security-driven additions with immediate notice.
3) Data transfers: we will include SCCs for EU-origin data in the DPA, or customers can opt for private deployment.

I propose the following course: accept most redlines with the auditor clause constrained as above, provide SOC2 summary and pen-test summary (redacted), and prepare a DocuSign envelope for the agreed DPA.

Attachments for internal review: Redwood_DPA_redline_response.docx (summary), SOC2-TypeII-Report-2026-summary.pdf, pen-test-summary-2026-redacted.txt

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_DPA_redline_response.docx]
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 08:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: DPA - initial redlines + audit scope question

A few privacy-specific calls out:
- Subprocessor addendum: recommend we include a short addendum describing our subprocessor onboarding and attestations (SOC2 or equivalent) rather than a free-form auditor right over subprocessors.
- Data export controls: if Aventis will transfer EU personal data, confirm they want SCCs or will handle through private deployment. If SCCs, we should add a standard data transfer exhibit referencing the SCCs and our subprocessors that may be outside the EEA.
- Retention/Deletion: their retention windows are slightly longer than our defaults; propose we keep their requested retention where it's justified by the state of the product but add an operational SLA to confirm deletion timing.

If we accept Marissa's constraints we should be good. I can prepare the subprocessor inventory CSV for them to review.

Karthik Iyer
Head of Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Aventis Legal <contracts@aventis-health.com>, Daniel Park <daniel.park@aventis-health.com>

Date: Tue, 9 Mar 2027 16:48:00 -08:00

- Auditor access limited to 1x per 12 months, scoped and with NDA
- Subprocessor notice: 21 days standard, emergency addition clause for security
- SCCs included for EU-origin personal data

Per our earlier notes, please review the DPA and sign via DocuSign using the envelope link below. Once signed we will deliver:
- SOC 2 Type II summary (attached) and full report under NDA
- Redacted penetration test summary (attached)
- Export of current subprocessor inventory (CSV)

Drive folder (read-only): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0B-example-dpa-evidence

Best regards,
Neha Kapoor
